official.name: Karsh International Scholars Program
official.host_org: Duke University (Office of Undergraduate Financial Aid)

verification.funding_note: No fixed dollar amount is published; the award is need-based and individualized to each scholar's financial circumstances.
verification.covered_expenses: Tuition, room and board, mandatory fees, demonstrated financial need exceeding those costs, and three summers of funding for research, unpaid internships, and other opportunities that advance the scholar's academic career.
eligibility: Students who are citizens of any country outside the United States, including dual citizens (students who are dual citizens of the US and another country may not apply)
First-year applicants to Duke University only
No nomination required; apply to Duke and request financial aid
required_docs: Request for financial aid as part of the Duke application process (no separate Karsh application or nomination)
verification.application_process: Apply to Duke University as a first-year student and request financial aid; there is no separate application or nomination for the Karsh program. Duke's admissions/financial aid offices review applicants for the scholarship within the regular admission and aid review cycle.
verification.contact_info: Duke University Office of Undergraduate Financial Aid, ousf.duke.edu
verification.status_note: Verified on ousf.duke.edu (Karsh International Scholars Program page), retrieved 2026-10-10. The program was established in 2010 by Martha L. and Bruce A. Karsh. The published benefits statement lists tuition, room and board, mandatory fees, demonstrated need exceeding those costs, plus three summers of funding; no separate application deadline, duration in years, travel allowance or renewal rule is published on the program page, so those fields remain null.

applicant_utility.exciting_but_honest_wins: Of all the international full-funding routes into an elite US university, this is the one with the cleanest targeting: no nomination, no essay about being global citizens - just apply to Duke, show need, and the package covers tuition, room, board and mandatory fees, then tops up whatever need remains, and funds three summers for research, unpaid internships or other academic enrichment. Three fully funded summers is the feature nobody advertises enough: for an international student, one unpaid internship summer in the US would otherwise be unaffordable.
applicant_utility.good_fit_if: You are a non-US citizen without US dual citizenship, you are finishing secondary school, you have never held a bachelor's degree, and your family genuinely cannot fund a US private university education. It fits if you are comfortable having your family finances examined in detail - this is a need-based award, not a merit prize - and if you already have internships or research summers mapped out for freshman through senior year.
applicant_utility.potential_drawbacks: Because it is need-based, a family with comfortable means will see little or no funding, and need is reassessed over four years - a change in family circumstances changes the award. There is no separate application, which is convenient but also means zero visibility: you will not know you are under consideration until an offer arrives, and no travel allowance or renewal rule is published on the program page, so confirm details with Duke's financial aid office.
document_checklist: Duke first-year (Common App or QuestBridge) application by the applicable Duke deadline
Financial aid request: FAFSA-equivalent/CSS Profile per Duke's aid instructions for international applicants
Parent income and asset documentation as Duke Financial Aid requests
No Karsh-specific forms, essays or references needed
applicant_utility.playbook_for_working_applicants: Your single lever is the financial aid application: file it as early and completely as Duke allows, because the Karsh is decided from your aid file alongside the admission review, not from a separate essay. Do not hold US dual citizenship and assume eligibility - dual citizens of the US and another country are explicitly barred. In the Duke application, make the summers concrete: a Karsh narrative writes itself when your activities show a through-line of research and internships you intend to pursue each summer. Finally, accept that the amount is individualized: map your family's ability to pay honestly before you apply, and ask Duke Financial Aid how the three-summer funding is allocated across the four years so you can plan internship applications.
